comparisons.peer_topic: Client CPU product launches and performance
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, Intel launched Intel Core Ultra Series 1 (first with integrated NPU for AI workloads) and the power-efficient Intel Core Ultra 200V Series. Additionally, the 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors continued to serve a significant majority of client sales.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Intel are explicitly launching new commercial client CPU series in 2024 that integrate dedicated AI processing units to drive 'AI PC' capabilities. AMD launched the 'Ryzen AI PRO 300 series' which brings 'AI capabilities to business notebooks', while Intel launched the 'Intel Core Ultra Series 1', described as the 'first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload' and introducing the 'first AI PCs to the market'. Both companies frame these launches around enhancing productivity and performance for commercial/business clients through integrated AI hardware.

sentences.text: We launched our AMD Ryzen AI PRO 300 series, bringing world-class security and manageability and leadership productivity, battery life, and AI capabilities to business notebooks and mobile workstations.

▪Client CPUs. In 2024, we ramped sales of the Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 1, our first product with an integrated neural processing unit for efficient processing of AI workload. The Intel Core Ultra Series 1, manufactured on the Intel 4 process, introduced the first AI PCs to the market. We also launched the Intel Core Ultra 200V Series, showcasing power efficiency and long-lasting battery life. The 200V Series, manufactured by an external foundry, leverages our Xe2 GPU architecture, bringing improved efficiency, second-generation ray tracing units and XMX AI acceleration to thin and light notebooks. During 2024, a significant majority of our client sales consisted of our 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, manufactured on Intel 7, which allow us to serve the breadth of customer and computing needs in the client market.

peer_results.rationale: Micron's candidates discuss storage (SSDs) required for next-gen AI PCs and data center AI workloads. While related to the PC market trend, the topic is storage components rather than the client CPU solutions and processor launches that define AMD's disclosure.

NVIDIA's candidates focus on enterprise AI software licensing (AI Enterprise) and historical R&D innovations (GPU, CUDA, Tensor Cores). These topics concern data center software and general AI infrastructure history, not the specific commercial client CPU product launches for business notebooks and workstations disclosed by AMD.

comparisons.peer_summary: Consumer IoT products are adopting latest mobile connectivity and on-device AI capabilities, with new AI-focused PCs launching in 2024 and analysts expecting 50% of PCs sold to be AI capable by 2027.
comparisons.comparison: Both AMD and Qualcomm identify the launch of new AI-focused PCs in 2024 as a key commercial and consumer driver. AMD discloses the launch of 'AMD Ryzen AI PRO 300 series' for 'business notebooks and mobile workstations' emphasizing leadership productivity and AI capabilities. Similarly, Qualcomm highlights that 'a new class of AI-focused PCs, including those powered by our Snapdragon X Series platforms, launched in 2024', enabling on-device AI processing. Both disclosures underscore the shift toward AI-enabled personal computing devices in the current fiscal year.
